summary: The visit that goes wrong: {powerful officeholder} came to campaign beside you, and at {the stop} the crowd turns on you both.
realLife: In the 1983 Chicago general election, protesters confronted Washington and former Vice President Walter Mondale outside St. Pascal's church on the Northwest Side. The campaign later used footage of them in ads aimed at white liberals.
gates: A visit by {powerful officeholder} on the calendar.
A stop in an area that opposes you.
choices: use the footage of the crowd in an ad

branches.then: It can reach voters put off by the crowd. Using it writes an ad record and costs you the stop's voters for good.
They say you chose the stop, and the next visit is harder to get.
